title: Add Quickstart default dashboards + alert rules (telemetry contract v1) and import docs
author: Sergio Costa
body: Context: Quickstart templates are standardizing on Telemetry Contract v1 (traces/metrics/log fields). This PR adds an out-of-the-box “observability pack” in the observability-pack repo: dashboards + alert rules that assume the contract’s metric names/trace attributes and are safe by default (low-noise, burn-rate oriented). This is intended to be imported by users running templates locally (Grafana/Prometheus/OTel Collector) and by internal teams validating the templates against staging. What’s included: 1) Dashboards (Grafana JSON): - Quickstart Overview: request volume, error rate (by error_class), p50/p95 latency, token usage + estimated cost, and saturation panels. - RAG Deep Dive: retrieval latency, embed latency, vector DB errors/timeouts, doc ingestion throughput (if enabled), and cache hit ratio (when emitted). - Agent/Tools Deep Dive: tool call counts, tool duration, tool timeout rate, tool error_class breakdown, and “model vs tool time” stacked visualization. - 429/Rate Limits: rate limit responses, backoff/retry patterns (derived from SDK retry metrics), and guidance panels linking to template docs. 2) Alert rules (Grafana unified alerting YAML + JSON exports): - High error burn: 5m and 1h windows (multi-window, multi-burn) on error rate excluding canceled requests. - Latency burn: p95 > SLO thresholds with long-window confirmation to avoid noise on low traffic. - Excess 429s: alerts only when sustained above a baseline AND request volume > N to reduce false positives during dev. - Tool timeout spike: only for routes tagged with template.kind=agents or template.kind=rag_agent. - Collector ingestion gap (optional): for setups that deploy the provided OTel Collector config (not required). 3) Import instructions + compatibility notes: - README explains required metric names and labels, recommended OTel Collector config (example snippet), and how to map request_id / tenant_id into logs for correlation. - Includes “cardinality guardrails” section: templates must not emit arbitrary user IDs into labels; dashboards are built around bounded attributes (route, model, deployment_mode, error_class, template_name, template_version). Notes/assumptions: - Metric names follow telemetry contract v1 (e.g., redwood.request.count, redwood.request.latency_ms, redwood.tokens.total, redwood.errors.count, redwood.tools.duration_ms). - Alerts use error_class (timeout, rate_limited, upstream, validation, tool_error, canceled, unknown) instead of raw status codes where possible. - Dashboards support Hosted API and Dedicated/Private deployments by filtering on deployment_mode and region when present. Changed areas/files (high level): - packs/quickstart/v1/dashboards/quickstart-overview.json - packs/quickstart/v1/dashboards/rag-deep-dive.json - packs/quickstart/v1/dashboards/agents-tools-deep-dive.json - packs/quickstart/v1/dashboards/429-and-retries.json - packs/quickstart/v1/alerts/quickstart-alerts.yaml - packs/quickstart/v1/alerts/quickstart-alerts.json - packs/quickstart/v1/README.md - packs/quickstart/v1/examples/otel-collector-config.yaml - tooling/validate-pack.ts (ensures dashboards only reference allowed label keys + required metrics exist) - .github/workflows/ci.yml (pack validation step) Implementation details: - Added a small validation script that parses the dashboard JSON and alert rule expressions to check: (a) metric names are in the allow-list for contract v1, (b) label keys are bounded (no user.*, email, etc.), (c) all dashboards include template_name and template_version variables. - Alerts default to “no data = OK” for dev friendliness, except collector ingestion gap (no data = alert) when explicitly enabled. - Added “Console deep link” panels as markdown annotations where applicable (these are placeholders for users on Hosted API; internal teams can replace base URL via env var). Test plan: - CI: validate-pack, lint, and JSON schema checks for Grafana exports. - Local: imported into Grafana 10.2 against a Prometheus test fixture that replays sample metrics from quickstart smoke tests. - Staging: verified expected panels populate when running redwood-quickstarts smoke tests (ENG-2848) with telemetry enabled. Rollout: - No production changes; this repo is consumed by docs and template repos. - After merge, we will tag v0.3.0 of observability-pack and update redwood-quickstarts to reference that tag (tracked in ENG-2846 follow-up). Screenshots: attached in PR comments (Overview + Agents/Tools dashboards) to validate layout and variable wiring. Related: - Telemetry contract: ENG-2845 - Template docs: ENG-2850 - Default dashboards spec in Confluence: “quickstart-default-dashboards”
commits: Add quickstart v1 Grafana dashboards (overview, RAG, agents/tools, 429s)
Add unified alerting rules with burn-rate style thresholds and low-noise defaults
Add pack README with import steps and cardinality guidance
Add pack validation tooling + CI step
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Dashboard variables look good; can you confirm we’re not encouraging high-cardinality labels (tenant_id) in Prometheus labels? Author (Sergio): Yep — tenant_id is only referenced as a log field / trace attr; dashboards use bounded labels only. Added explicit callout in README under Cardinality guardrails. Logan Wright: Alert expressions should key on error_class rather than status_code where possible. Also, 429 alert feels noisy for low traffic. Author: Updated to use error_class=rate_limited and added request volume gate (> 2 rps over 10m) + multi-window burn rate. Rafael Mendes: For dev setups, please ensure “no data” doesn’t page people. Especially for latency and error alerts. Author: Set “no data = OK” across the default alert group; only the optional collector ingestion alert uses “no data = alert” and is disabled by default via folder selection. Aisha Bello: Can we add a small “expected baseline” note for p95 during template smoke tests so people don’t assume regressions? Author: Added a note panel in Overview with typical staging ranges and a link to ENG-2848. Dylan Brooks: Any way to add Console deep links in a way that doesn’t confuse OSS users? Author: Added as markdown panels with a clearly marked placeholder base URL and a toggle variable “show_console_links” default false. Approvals: Allison ✅, Logan ✅, Rafael ✅
release_notes: Observability pack: added Quickstart Templates v1 dashboards (overview, RAG, agents/tools, 429s) and low-noise default alert rules aligned to Telemetry Contract v1. Includes import instructions and validation tooling to prevent high-cardinality label usage.
